shapes.text: DETAIL 1   EAVE — DRIP EDGE + PANEL HEM
SECTION, TRUE SCALE. Shown flat; the roof actually falls 2 in 12 to the left.

shapes.label: Snap-lock panel 26ga, hemmed at the eave

shapes.text: 24" o.c. — the skip boards set your clip spacing
PANEL EAVE HEM — no fasteners here
Cut the panel 1" long. Fold that inch
UNDER with a hand seamer, then hook it
over the drip edge hem and press home.
Two hooks locked together is what holds
the eave down in wind.
F15H556 HEM FLAT — goes on FIRST
Covers the 2x6 fascia. Its 1.5" hem
means no raw cut edge shows at the
bottom. Top flange lands on the deck
and gets buried by the drip edge.
SSDE6 DRIP EDGE
Top flange screwed to the skip board,
1" wafers at 12" o.c. Outer edge is
hemmed and opens up-slope — that hem
is what the panel grabs.
Butyl tape in the hem is REQUIRED on this
roof — 2:12 is below the usual 3:12 minimum.

shapes.label: 5" K gutter (hangs on the fascia, under the drip edge)

shapes.text: gutter hangs BELOW the drip edge lip
DETAIL 2   ENDWALL — WHERE THE ROOF MEETS THE HOUSE
SECTION, TRUE SCALE. Down-slope is to the left. Highest-risk joint on the job.

shapes.label: SS1Z6 1" Z closure at the headwall
1" wafer screw through the Z into the skip board

shapes.text: 6" min. up the wall
PANEL TURN-UP — 1", the first dam
Cut the panel 1" long at the top and bend
the end straight up with a turn-up tool.
This is what stops wind-driven water from
running back down under the panel.
EFC1925 FOAM CLOSURE — check this one
Seats in front of the Z leg. Only 2 pcs were
ordered (~38 in total); a 24 ft headwall wants
the whole run. Call the supplier before you
start — this is the piece to get right.
SS1Z6 — 1" Z CLOSURE
Bottom flange screws to the SKIP BOARD,
never through the panel. Leg stands up
behind the turn-up as a second dam. Top
flange gives the endwall metal a landing.
SSEW6 ENDWALL FLASHING
Vertical leg runs at least 6" up the wall,
tucked BEHIND the housewrap and siding.
Never caulk it to the face of the siding.
Roof leg lands on the Z over butyl tape.
DETAIL 3   RAKE — THE GABLE EDGE
SECTION cut across the panels, TRUE SCALE. Roof field is to the right.

shapes.label: Last panel, cut to width, edge turned up 1"
SS1Z6 1" Z used as a rake cleat
1" wafer screw, Z cleat to deck
rivet, rake trim into the Z, 16" o.c.

shapes.text: ORDER OF ASSEMBLY, BOTTOM UP
1.  Cut the last panel to width, turn the cut edge up 1".
2.  Z cleat screwed to the deck just OUTBOARD of that
turn-up: leg up, top flange toward the rake edge.
3.  Rake trim drops over and is riveted DOWN into the
Z's top flange — the face of the rake stays clean.
4.  Hemmed bottom edge closes off the 2x6 rake board.
The rake trim covers about 1" of panel. On an 18-panel
exact fit, that hidden inch at each rake is your ONLY
tolerance — roughly 2 in total across 24 ft.
DETAIL 4   THE SNAP-LOCK SEAM + CONCEALED CLIP
SECTION across two panels at a skip board, TRUE SCALE.

shapes.label: 1" wafer screw (WFS1MTW) through clip into skip board

shapes.text: 1" seam
16" net coverage  |  18 panels = 288" = 24'-0" exactly
HOW THE SEAM LOCKS
1.  Panel A is set; its MALE leg stands 1" tall.
2.  A clip hooks over that male leg at every skip
board and takes one 1" wafer screw.
3.  Panel B's FEMALE leg comes down over both and
you walk the seam closed with your palm. It SNAPS —
listen for it, the whole length, top to bottom.
4.  Nothing penetrates a panel anywhere in the field.
DETAIL 5   TRIM END LAP
ELEVATION — how two 10'2" sticks of trim join. TRUE SCALE.

shapes.label: trim stick — DOWN-slope, goes on first
butyl tape, full width of the lap

shapes.text: 6" lap
RULES FOR EVERY LAP ON THIS ROOF
-  The UP-SLOPE piece always laps OVER the down-slope piece.
Running water must never meet an upstream edge.
-  6" lap minimum, butyl tape the full width of the lap.
-  Two rivets top, two bottom, through both layers.
-  Notch the hem back 1" on the covering piece so the two
hems nest instead of fighting each other.
-  3 sticks of 10'2" across 24 ft leaves 6'6" for laps and waste.
Mark both lap positions BEFORE you cut anything.
DETAIL 6   EAVE / RAKE CORNER
PLAN — the order the pieces stack. Never improvise this corner.

shapes.label: 1. fascia flat runs through the corner
2. eave drip edge laps over the fascia flat
3. rake trim runs DOWN over the drip edge

shapes.text: CORNER SEQUENCE
Fascia flat first, drip edge over it, rake LAST.
At the corner, run the rake trim 2" past the drip edge,
notch the vertical leg, and fold the tab DOWN over the
drip edge face. Bed it in butyl, one rivet, done.
A cut-and-caulk corner is the number one callback on
a metal roof — caulk is a maintenance item, a fold is not.
SNAP-LOCK STANDING SEAM — TRIM & INTERLOCK DETAILS
Beard's Home Services  |  Covered patio — 24'-0" wide x 9'-3" slope, 2:12 shed roof
Charcoal Crinkle 26ga  |  18 panels at 16" net coverage  |  every detail drawn TRUE SCALE, in inches
READ THIS BEFORE THE FIRST PANEL GOES ON
2:12 sits BELOW the 3:12 minimum that most snap-lock profiles are rated for. Confirm with the supplier that
this profile is approved at 2:12. If it is not, the roof needs full self-adhered underlayment wall-to-wall plus
butyl in every seam and every hem — or a mechanically-seamed panel instead of snap-lock.
18 panels at 16" is 288" — exactly 24'-0", with no spare and no cut panel. Measure the eave before you
unload. Chalk a control line every 64" (4 panels) and check your module at every line.
Panels were ordered at 9'-3"; the framing plan shows a 9'-6" run. Verify on site — you need length for the
eave hem and the headwall turn-up, and the panels as ordered may be short.
